groups.title: Monitoring & Control
groups.description: See and steer every printer in real time, from a single dashboard.

items.title: Live status via WebSocket
items.body: Temperatures, fans, layer count, AMS, current job - all push-updated, no polling.

items.title: Motion control, the way Studio does it
items.body: A round pad for the toolhead with 10 mm and 1 mm rings and Home in the middle, the nozzle-bed gap beside it, and manual extrude / retract with the extruder drawn from Bambu Studio's own artwork. BamDude reads which axes the printer says are homed rather than guessing, and refuses a cold extruder below 170 degrees - grinding a flat onto the filament is not a mistake worth making twice.

items.title: Set temperatures, not just read them
items.body: Nozzle, bed and chamber, both nozzles on dual-nozzle machines, with the limits your printer actually reports. An X1 on 220 V mains accepts a lower bed temperature than one on 110 V, and the chamber ceiling differs per model - so the number in front of you is the number the machine will honour. Zero always means off.

items.title: Fan and air-duct control on every printer
items.body: Per-fan speeds, air-duct mode and filtration, each fan labelled the way your own machine names it. Printers that describe no air duct at all - P1S, P1P, X1C, A1 - used to show three read-only numbers; they now get the same working controls, built from what they do report.

items.title: A timelapse is never promised to a printer that cannot record it
items.body: The tick used to go to any printer, including one with no card in it - the request went nowhere and the print finished with no video and no explanation. Now a machine that cannot record is named when you pick printers, with which of three problems it has, and a queue whose printer has run out of room pauses instead of quietly dropping the recording. Printers with internal storage or a timelapse kit are never asked about the card at all.

items.title: Multi-printer dashboard
items.body: Resizable cards, group by location, jump to any printer in one click.

items.title: Print progress in the browser tab
items.body: Optional, per browser. The tab title carries the percentage of the print finishing soonest and the tab icon becomes a matching progress ring in your accent colour — a window parked on another screen tells you how the farm is doing without switching to it.

items.title: Custom sidebar links + drag-to-reorder
items.body: Admins add wiki / helpdesk / Grafana / external printer links directly into the sidebar, scoped to one of six nav groups (Operations / Workshop / Resources / Care / System / Links). Drag-and-drop reorder within a group or move whole groups as a block — never accidentally scramble the grouping.

items.title: Camera streaming
items.body: Live MJPEG and snapshots, plus optional RTSP/USB external cameras.

items.title: Camera Wall
items.body: Flip the Printers page to Cam wall and watch every printer's camera in one live grid — or open it at its own /camwall URL to bookmark it or pin it to a wall-mounted screen. On-screen tiles stream live (capped so a Raspberry Pi keeps up), off-screen ones pause, and each tile carries a status overlay + HMS badge. A TV or Pi with no login runs it with a Cam Wall token, which serves only what a tile draws — never a printer's address or the name of the file being printed.

items.title: In-app camera diagnostics
items.body: A Diagnose button on the camera viewer runs a staged check — network reachability then a real first-frame capture — and shows exactly which stage failed with a plain-language fix-it hint, so a 'camera broken' problem resolves on screen instead of in a support ticket.

items.title: Long-lived camera tokens
items.body: Mint multi-year tokens for Home Assistant / Frigate / kiosk dashboards instead of renewing per-session 60-min ones. Three separate scopes — camera stream, Cam Wall, streaming overlay — that never widen one another, so a token handed out for video can't enumerate your fleet or read what's on the bed.

items.title: OBS overlay
items.body: Drop a single URL into OBS for a clean live-stream overlay with progress, ETA, and AMS. OBS has no login session, so it authenticates with a Streaming Overlay token — one printer, nothing else.

items.title: Calibration UI
items.body: Bed leveling, vibration, motor noise, nozzle offset, high-temp heatbed - model-aware, from web or Telegram.

items.title: Printer Settings dialog
items.body: Bambu Studio parity — toggle ~15 print-time behaviours from the kebab menu: AI failure detections with Low/Medium/High sensitivity (spaghetti, pile-up, clumping, air-print, first-layer, monitoring), FOD + displacement, filament-tangle, nozzle-blob, open-door check (Off/Pause/Halt), purify air (Off/Inside/Outside), auto-recovery, prompt sound, snapshot, save-remote, plate marker + alignment. Per-model gating hides what your printer doesn't support; every change audited to printer_setting_audit.

items.title: HMS error decoding
items.body: Translates Bambu's numeric error codes to plain language with per-printer history — and surfaces the same fix-it buttons the printer's own screen offers (Resume, Stop, Ignore & Resume, Stop Drying…), one click straight to the printer.

items.title: Air-duct fans on the P2S and X2D
items.body: The second auxiliary fan — an add-on kit on the P2S, factory-fitted on the X2D — is never reported as a plain speed field, so nothing could show it. It now appears as its own badge with its speed, and you can set that speed from the badge. Names come from Bambu Studio's own printer definitions, so the same position reads Left on a P2S and Right on an X2D.

items.title: AMS management
items.body: Slot config, RFID re-read, load / unload from the printer card, AMS Settings dialog (Bambu Studio parity — RFID auto-read on insert/power-on, remaining-capacity estimate, filament backup, air-print detection, AMS calibrate, A1 firmware FULL↔LITE switch, H2D AMS reorder), drying schedules, humidity tracking.

items.title: Printer file browser
items.body: Browse the printer's SD card, bulk-download or bulk-delete remote files. Save-to-Library promotes bare .3mf to .gcode.3mf when the bytes are already sliced.

items.title: LAN firmware updates
items.body: Fetch Bambu firmware from the CDN, push to the printer's SD card over LAN-mode FTP, apply from the printer screen — no cloud account. Update one printer or the whole farm at once: the Firmware page groups printers by model, downloads each firmware once, pushes in parallel, skips mid-print printers, and keeps a per-run update log. A durable local store keeps every version (so you can roll back even after Bambu pulls it). curl_cffi Chrome impersonation handles Cloudflare's JA3 gate; stale buildId self-heals.

items.title: Mobile / PWA install
items.body: Install BamDude as a PWA on iOS, Android, or desktop — standalone window, offline app shell, share-target uploads (Android), push notifications when HTTPS is on.

groups.title: Print farm queue
groups.description: Per-printer queues with parallel dispatch, staggered start, and built-in SWAP-mode support.

items.title: Parallel background dispatch
items.body: Send jobs to multiple printers simultaneously - startup-locked DB phase, parallel FTP and start.

items.title: Per-printer queues
items.body: Each printer has its own ordered queue with idle/printing/paused/error tracking.

items.title: Group, drag-reorder & sort by ETA
items.body: Tame a long queue: bundle items into a collapsible batch, drag a row by its grip handle to reorder, and sort the Printers page by ETA so the printer finishing next sits on top.

items.title: Auto-queue routing
items.body: Drop a print without naming a target - the router picks a suitable printer by model, filament type, and (optionally) color, preferring one that can start right away. SJF + starvation guard for fair scheduling.

items.title: Auto-pause on failure
items.body: When a print fails, the queue stops on that printer so you can decide what's next.

items.title: Cancel-during-dispatch pauses (not errors)
items.body: Cancelling during the upload/start window moves the queue to paused (not error) and the item to cancelled (not failed) — nothing failed, you just changed your mind. A Restart button on the cancelled item puts it back at the end of the queue with one click.

items.title: Staggered start
items.body: Limit concurrent heating across the farm - bed temp watchdog prevents brownouts.

items.title: Re-print with AMS mapping
items.body: Reprint to any printer, remap each filament slot from the source archive.

items.title: Swap mode (A1 plate-swappers)
items.body: Built-in support for Kit / STL / JobOx swappers with macro-driven plate changes.

items.title: G-code macros with ACK
items.body: Send macros from the printer card; MQTT-confirmed completion, real-time status.

items.title: Quick vibration check toggle
items.body: Per-job toggle that comments out M970 in 3MF gcode and recalculates MD5 sidecars.

items.title: G-code injection per print
items.body: Per-printer-model snippet library; toggle Inject G-code on a job to splice start/end snippets directly into the plate gcode.

items.title: Slice settings
items.body: Save a slice setup once — printer + process + per-slot filament presets + bed type — then load all four back into the Slice dialog with a single pick instead of choosing them again. A preset that has since been deleted is never applied silently: the affected slot keeps its automatic pick and is named in a warning, so you never slice with something you did not choose. Printing a batch is the auto-queue's job, not the pipeline's.

items.title: Preheat & heat-soak
items.body: Hold the bed — and, on chamber-equipped printers, the chamber — at temperature before an engineering-filament job starts: the soak ABS / ASA / PA / PC need that Bambu firmware won't wait for. The chamber target derives per print from the loaded AMS filament types (editable map), and three hardware tiers are handled automatically — active M141 heater (H2 series / X2D / X1E), sensor-only radiant wait (X1C / P2S), or a soak timer (P1S / A1). Off by default, with a per-print override in the Print dialog.

groups.title: Print archive
groups.description: Every print kept locally with the source 3MF and full metadata. Searchable forever.

items.title: Automatic 3MF archiving
items.body: Every print stored with metadata, thumbnail, gcode hash, and runtime data.

items.title: Three.js 3D viewer
items.body: Inspect every plate in-browser with multi-color preview before reprinting.

items.title: Build-plate icon on archive cards
items.body: Every card shows an OrcaSlicer-style bed icon next to the printer / model name reflecting the plate the 3MF was sliced for (Cool / SuperTack / Engineering / High Temp / Textured PEI / Smooth PEI). Hover tooltip carries the full name — no need to open the source 3MF in a slicer just to read the bed setting before a re-print.

items.title: Full-text search & dedup
items.body: Source-hash chain-of-custody so patched files (e.g. M970-disabled) still dedup correctly.

items.title: Photo attachments & notes
items.body: Attach failure photos, post-process pics, freeform notes per archive.

items.title: Side-by-side compare
items.body: Compare 2–5 prints (settings, filament, time, weight) in one view.

items.title: Timelapse editor
items.body: Trim, speed, add music - export ready-to-share clips from raw camera footage.

items.title: Auto-cleanup retention
items.body: Drop the .3mf after N days idle, keep the metadata, thumbnail, energy, and notes.

items.title: Library + Archive Trash bins
items.body: Soft-delete with restore window, scheduled retention, and reference-aware delete that refuses to drop bytes still pinned by an active archive.

items.title: Printed / Not Printed filters
items.body: One-click chips on the archive page split first-time prints from reprints — fast path to find never-printed files.

items.title: 3MF download recovery
items.body: Failed FTP at print start? Recovery retries on startup, reconnect, print-end, or manually.

items.title: Failure analysis dashboard
items.body: Retrospective analytics across the archive — failure rate by printer, material, time-of-day, and print duration. Drill into the offending archives in one click.

items.title: CSV / XLSX export
items.body: Filter-aware bulk export of archives + stats for billing, QA logs, or BI pipelines. UTF-8 BOM CSV, multi-sheet XLSX.

groups.title: File Library
groups.description: Upload, organize, and print directly - no slicer round-trip required.

items.title: Upload & folder organize
items.body: Drag-and-drop folder structure with duplicate detection on hash.

items.title: Per-plate gallery
items.body: Multi-plate sliced 3MFs show every plate with its own stats, filament, and object list.

items.title: STL thumbnails
items.body: Thumbnail-render STL on upload so you see the part, not a filename.

items.title: External folder mounting
items.body: Mount a NAS share or USB drive read-only into the library.

items.title: Print directly or queue
items.body: Pick a file, pick a printer (model-filtered), print now or add to queue.

items.title: Schedule a whole selection
items.body: Tick any number of sliced files and press Schedule: the usual scheduling window opens for the first, marked 1/3, then the next. Each file keeps the full set of choices — printers or the auto-queue, plates, filament mapping, options, quantity, when to start. Close it at any point and whatever you did not get to stays selected.

items.title: Label-objects metadata
items.body: Skip-objects support detected at upload - button only enables when the slicer's profile actually emits it.

items.title: MakerWorld URL import
items.body: Paste any MakerWorld model URL, pick a plate, BamDude downloads the 3MF straight into your library — provenance badge keeps the link back to the original.

items.title: MakerWorld History tab + per-variant dedupe
items.body: Server-paginated 4-column grid of every MakerWorld import with locally-cached cover images, search across filename/title/author, sort by date/title/author, and a per-variant 'already imported' badge with a one-click View-in-Library deep-link on the resolve preview — never pay a duplicate download.

items.title: MakerWorld Re-download
items.body: Author pushed an update? Re-download overwrites the 3MF bytes + cover + metadata in place. library_file_id stays stable so queue items, project links, and archives keep resolving to the same row.

items.title: MakerWorld design metadata captured
items.body: Title, author, license, sliced-for printer, full compatibility list, materials, AMS requirement, and a deep-link back to the original — all written to a child meta table on import and used to drive the History grid.

items.title: Server-side slicing
items.body: Send STL/3MF to a containerised OrcaSlicer or BambuStudio sidecar and get a printable .gcode.3mf back without leaving the app.

items.title: Re-slice for any printer
items.body: Re-slice a saved 3MF for a different printer — even across nozzle classes (single ↔ dual-nozzle H2D/H2C/X2D). Pick the target profile and BamDude arranges the objects for the new bed; 'slice all plates' merges a multi-plate project into one file.

items.title: Keep the designer's print settings
items.body: MakerWorld models often deviate from the stock profile on purpose — five walls, 100% infill, a 0.1 mm first layer — and a re-slice used to throw all of it away. The Slice dialog now lists exactly which settings the author changed, with a checkbox each: design intent ticked, machine-tuned values (speeds, accelerations, temperatures) listed but not. Bambu Studio writes that list into the 3MF itself, so nothing is guessed.

items.title: Slicer Preset Bundles (.bbscfg)
items.body: Import a BambuStudio Printer Preset Bundle once and reference its triplets (printer + process + filament) by name on every slice — bypasses the cloud / local / standard tier resolution entirely. Idempotent re-uploads keyed on bundle hash; per-bundle Settings panel for delete.

items.title: Per-user Bambu Cloud
items.body: Each user signs into their own Bambu Cloud account with their own region — no shared credentials, no single-region lock-in. Tokens encrypted at rest, sliding refresh, OIDC-style flow.

items.title: Orca Cloud profile sync
items.body: Sign into OrcaSlicer's cloud (Supabase sync) alongside Bambu Cloud and your synced printer / process / filament profiles show up in the slice modal and AMS-slot picker — ranked above Bambu Cloud, local, and standard. Full metadata inline, so filament type and colour pre-fill for free. Google / Apple / GitHub / email sign-in via a paste-based PKCE flow. Per-user tokens, just-in-time refresh.

items.title: Local OrcaSlicer presets
items.body: Drop .orca_filament / .bbscfg / .bbsflmt / ZIP bundles directly — BamDude resolves preset inheritance from upstream OrcaSlicer when needed. Cloud-free path for shops without Bambu accounts.

items.title: Links that say what they do, and links that stay unique
items.body: Linking a library folder to an archive puts an "open source folder" shortcut on that archive - and nothing on the folder, which is why the field never explained itself. It does now. It is also one archive to one folder: claiming one another folder already holds is refused by name, instead of quietly taking it away from a folder you are not looking at. Archived projects, meanwhile, have left the pickers entirely - except where something is already linked to one, which stays visible so saving the dialog cannot erase it.

items.title: A printed file can go back into the library
items.body: Asked for by a user. Pick a folder and the archive's 3MF is copied in, read the same way an upload is — metadata, thumbnail, per-plate details and badges already filled in, rather than an anonymous file. Saving the same print twice does not make a second copy: the library recognises identical content, keeps the one already there, and says so.

groups.title: Telegram bot
groups.description: Full bot for control and queue management. Multi-chat, role-based.

items.title: Full printer control
items.body: Pause, resume, stop, light, speed, camera snapshot - all from chat.

items.title: Multi-chat with roles
items.body: Each Telegram chat gets a role with granular per-resource permissions.

items.title: Actionable buttons
items.body: Clear plate, mark maintenance done, pause/stop on progress - straight from the notification.

items.title: Print from Library
items.body: Browse files, pick a printer (model-filtered), Print Now or Add to Queue.

items.title: Queue management
items.body: Paginated list, detail view, move up/down, cancel - with MarkdownV2 formatting.

items.title: Add Printer via SSDP
items.body: Enter IP → bot auto-detects serial / name / model → enter access code → done.

items.title: Calibration from chat
items.body: Trigger bed leveling, vibration, nozzle offset, motor noise, high-temp heatbed.

items.title: Per-chat quiet hours
items.body: Daily digest, event filtering, and quiet-hour windows - independent per chat.

groups.title: Notifications
groups.description: Eight channels, one editor, one routing config.

items.title: 9 delivery channels
items.body: Telegram, Discord, Email (SMTP), Pushover, ntfy, Bark, CallMeBot, Home Assistant, custom webhooks.

items.title: Bark, for the failure at 3 a.m.
items.body: The free iOS push app that needs no account — install it, paste the device key. Its Critical interruption level is delivered through Silent mode and through Focus, so the print that stopped in the night actually wakes somebody; Time Sensitive breaks through scheduled summaries without going that far. Public relay or your own bark-server.

items.title: Home Assistant push options
items.body: A Data (JSON) field that goes straight into the service call, the same place an automation would put it — priority: high and ttl: 0 to arrive immediately rather than whenever the phone next wakes, channel to give printer alerts their own sound. Checked when you save it and again when it is sent.

items.title: MarkdownV2 template editor
items.body: Formatting toolbar, per-event template, live preview before saving.

items.title: Print-finish photo
items.body: Camera snapshot attached to the success notification, with filament usage details.

items.title: HMS + bed-cooled alerts
items.body: Get pinged when an HMS error fires or when the bed cools enough to remove the part.

items.title: Queue events
items.body: Notifications for waiting, skipped, failed - only the events you opt into.

items.title: Per-event ntfy priority
items.body: Pick the ntfy priority (default / high / urgent) per event type, so finished prints don't shout but failures do.

items.title: Pause / Resume with classified reason
items.body: RUNNING↔PAUSE transitions fire dedicated notifications carrying a normalised reason (door / filament runout / presence-check / file-pause / AI defect / plate-objects / user / HMS-other) and a paused-for counter on resume. Printer cards render a live PauseChip with the same reason + mm:ss ticker while paused — so you can tell at a glance whether the operator already knows.

groups.title: Spools & Projects
groups.description: Track filament inventory and group prints into projects.

items.title: Built-in spool inventory
items.body: Add spools with brand, color, weight, cost; AMS slot assignment per printer.

items.title: Mass actions on the Filament tab
items.body: Tick the spools you mean - a row, a whole group, the visible page, or everything matching the current filter - then Edit, Print labels, Reset usage, Archive, Restore or Delete them in one go. Works the same in built-in and Spoolman modes. Destructive actions confirm first, and the selection clears itself whenever the filter or tab changes, so a bulk delete can never land on rows you are no longer looking at.

items.title: Auto consumption tracking
items.body: Filament used per print is deducted from the assigned spool - no manual math.

items.title: Cost & lot tracking
items.body: Per-spool cost, purchase date, filament diameter, and lot number for inventory bundles.

items.title: Spoolman sync + first-class inventory UI
items.body: Two-way sync with Spoolman for shops that already keep inventory there. Plus a full BamDude-side inventory experience on Spoolman-mode installs: structured slot assignments per (printer, AMS, tray) survive reboots, K-profiles per spool round-trip across BamDude installs that share one Spoolman, and the storage_location column shows on every spool card.

items.title: Color catalog
items.body: Manufacturer-aware color name resolution (Bambu wins for matching hex).

items.title: Multi-colour filament gradients
items.body: Dual-colour spools render as hard-split bars (not a smooth blend), Multicolor renders as a conic colour-wheel pie, gradient stays a 135° linear blend, and Sparkle / Wood / Marble / Glow / Matte / Silk overlays paint visibly on inventory cards. Live preview in the spool form so you see the effect before save.

items.title: Printable PDF spool labels
items.body: Per-spool icon and bulk Print labels… header action. Six templates: AMS holder (74×33 mm), AMS holder (75×55 mm), 40×30 box label (DK/Brother roll), 62×29 box label (Brother PT/QL + Dymo), Avery L7160 A4 (21/sheet), Avery 5160 US Letter (30/sheet). Each label carries swatch + bold brand + material + hex colour code + the spool's display name (using your configured naming template) + a QR code that deep-links back into BamDude on phone scan.

items.title: Copy Spool
items.body: Duplicate a spool in one click: pre-fills the form with everything except weight_used (reset to 0). Source row untouched; the new row gets its own id. Works in both local and Spoolman modes.

items.title: Pre-load assignment (weigh-then-assign)
items.body: Assign a fresh spool to an AMS slot before loading the filament. The assignment persists immediately; the printer-side configuration auto-fires the moment the slot transitions to loaded (keyed on the AMS load state, so 3rd-party spools without readable RFID trigger the replay too). The toast tells you the configuration is pending, not lying about success — Bambu firmware silently drops filament-setting commands for unloaded slots.

items.title: Stock forecasting + Logistics view
items.body: Per-SKU reorder intelligence on top of the real consumption history. Exponentially-weighted daily-rate (30-day half-life), 95%-service-level safety stock, days-left projection, reorder-by date, and a top-5 stacked-area chart with ROP reference lines. Inline editors for lead-time, safety-margin (days|grams), alert snooze. Companion Shopping List tracks SKUs through pending → purchased → received and auto-creates stock spools on receipt. New notification toggles for reorder and stock-break alerts (currently UI-only). Hidden in Spoolman mode.

items.title: Spool form preset dropdown shows all printer/nozzle variants
items.body: All P1S / X1C / A1 variants of the same filament render as separate rows with the full @printer suffix visible, instead of collapsing into one. Local OrcaSlicer / BambuStudio profiles merge alongside cloud presets — earlier versions hid them whenever the user was logged into Bambu Cloud.

items.title: Per-spool category + low-stock
items.body: Tag spools by category (PETG / ABS / TPU…) and override the global low-stock threshold per spool.

items.title: Projects with print plan
items.body: Group prints by project; per-file copies with live filament/time/cost totals.

items.title: Project URL + cover image
items.body: Attach a MakerWorld / Printables / repo URL to a project plus a hero cover photo — surfaces on cards and the detail page.

items.title: ZIP / JSON export
items.body: Move a project between BamDude installs or back it up offsite.

groups.title: Filament Calibration
groups.description: A Bambu Studio-parity calibration wizard built right in — no other Bambu management tool runs the calibration tests for you.

items.title: Guided calibration wizard
items.body: Open it from any printer card's kebab menu: Pressure Advance (PA Line / PA Pattern / PA Tower), the Temperature / Volumetric Speed / VFA / Retraction towers, and the two-pass Flow Rate test — all walked through step by step with Bambu Studio parity. Lidar-driven Auto calibration is rolling out separately. A sibling Calibration History modal lists every stored result.

items.title: Sliced against your own presets
items.body: Not a canned, pre-sliced 3MF. For every mode the wizard slices the calibration scaffold against your active printer / process / filament presets through a connected OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio sidecar — exactly as the BS desktop wizard does — applying per-mode preset overrides (wall loops, line width, spiral mode, initial-layer speed) first. The sliced 3MF is FTP'd to the printer and run as a real print through the normal dispatch pipeline, so plate-change macros and chamber-light MQTT actions fire for calibration prints too.

items.title: Pressure Advance, end to end
items.body: PA Line / Pattern / Tower are wired slice → FTP → print → save dialog → K-profile. PA Pattern's comb + K-digit g-code and PA Line's numbered row stack are regenerated for the operator's own start/end/step via Python ports of BS's `CalibPressureAdvancePattern::generate_custom_gcodes` / `CalibPressureAdvanceLine::print_pa_lines`. The measured K is written to a calibration row, pushed to the printer's 16-slot K-profile history over MQTT, and bound to the AMS slot so the next print uses it automatically.

items.title: Temperature, Speed, VFA & Retraction towers with a result calculator
items.body: The Temperature tower steps the nozzle down 5 °C every 10 mm band (start/end seeded from the loaded filament's material); the Volumetric Speed and VFA towers ramp outer-wall speed up a spiral tower; the Retraction tower lengthens retraction every 1 mm of height up a two-pillar stringing test. The per-layer ramp is post-patched into the sliced g-code — it is a GUI-only engine flag the slicer sidecar can't carry. These are print-and-eyeball tests, so the finish step gives you a calculator: enter the measured height and BamDude applies the per-mode formula and shows the value to copy into your slicer. Save records it to the calibration history as a per-printer farm record.

items.title: Two-pass Flow Rate calibration
items.body: Calibrates the filament's flow ratio — the multiplier behind every extrusion move. Pass 1 prints 9 patches at modifiers ±20 % around your filament preset's current `filament_flow_ratio` (auto-prefilled from the picked preset; can be overridden to test from a fresh 1.0 without editing the slicer profile). You pick the smoothest patch and BamDude automatically slices, FTPs and runs pass 2 — 10 finer patches centred on the coarse pick. The two-pass dispatch is end-to-end; you never leave the wizard. The final ratio = `coarse × (100 + fine modifier) / 100` is saved to the calibration history as a per-(printer, filament, nozzle) record for the operator to copy into their slicer.

items.title: Per-printer cache, auto-bind, H2D dual-extruder
items.body: Results are keyed per (printer, filament, nozzle, extruder) — two identical X1Cs in a farm carry independent K values. The active calibration auto-binds on every print start by re-matching the printer's live cali_idx through stable identity, so AMS slot reorders and RFID re-taps can't silently fall back to the wrong K. H2D / H2D Pro calibrate each extruder on its own tab. The Calibration History modal does set-active / delete / refresh-from-printer per row.

groups.title: Maintenance
groups.description: Per-printer counters, model-aware tasks, mark done from anywhere.

items.title: Per-printer Maintenance Mode
items.body: Park a printer 'out of service' without deleting it — it drops out of queue dispatch, scheduling, auto-drying and metrics and shows an amber Maintenance pill until you bring it back. Toggle it from the printer's ⋮ menu.

items.title: Archive a printer
items.body: Retired a printer — sold, decommissioned, swapped out? Archive it instead of deleting: it vanishes from the Printers page, every picker, queues, dispatch and MQTT while its full print history is kept. Archiving is blocked mid-print and cancels the printer's pending queue items; restore it (or delete for good) under Settings → Printing. Distinct from Maintenance Mode, which only parks a printer temporarily.

items.title: Model-aware task types
items.body: Each printer model gets the maintenance items it actually has (e.g. carbon-rod wipe on X1).

items.title: Counters with overdue alerts
items.body: Hours-based + calendar-based reminders; UI badges and notifications.

items.title: Mark done from bot
items.body: Tap an actionable Telegram button to log the task - counters reset instantly.

items.title: History & Excel export
items.body: Every maintenance event logged with operator, date, hours; export to spreadsheet.

groups.title: Automation
groups.description: Smart plugs, virtual printer, AI failure detection - opt in to what you need.

items.title: Smart plug control
items.body: Zigbee, Tasmota, Home Assistant, MQTT, REST/webhook plugs - auto power on/off with prints.

items.title: Zigbee plugs, no bridge required
items.body: BamDude drives a Zigbee dongle itself - no Home Assistant, no Zigbee2MQTT, nothing running alongside. Pair a plug from the interface, bind it to a printer, and per-print energy comes from the plug's own meter.

items.title: Environment sensors on the same radio
items.body: Pair a Zigbee temperature/humidity sensor to the dongle already driving your plugs. Readings show in the sidebar and beside the printers standing in that place, with a week of history to chart.

items.title: Alerts when a room leaves its limits
items.body: Set a lowest and/or highest value for anything a sensor measures, including its own battery. You are told when a reading leaves those limits and again when it returns; a margin stops a value hovering on the line from ringing repeatedly. A sensor that stops reporting is reported too - otherwise a flat battery looks exactly like a quiet room.

items.title: Accessory plugs know their place
items.body: Mark which plug actually powers the printer. Switch off a chamber filter, a light or a dryer and the printer stays online and keeps taking work from the queue.

items.title: Energy tracking
items.body: Per-print kWh capture from the plug, plus date-range farm-wide totals.

items.title: Virtual printer modes
items.body: File Manager (review queue), Print Queue (slicer → fixed printer), Auto-Queue (slicer → router picks a suitable printer), Proxy (TLS relay). Per-VP, it can also keep the AMS slots the slicer resolved instead of matching by filament type and colour — the only way to tell two spools of the same colour apart.

items.title: Slicer-as-remote in non-proxy modes
items.body: When the VP has a target printer, the slicer sees real AMS / FTS / nozzle / k-profile state and streams the live camera through the VP — full slicer-as-remote without giving up BamDude's queue / archive / dispatch.

items.title: Live print progress in the slicer
items.body: The slicer's Device tab shows the target printer's real stage, percentage, layer and time remaining — and the Send button stays enabled throughout, so you can queue the next job while the current one prints.

items.title: Proxy mode for remote prints
items.body: Send from anywhere via TLS relay - no VPN, no port-forward, end-to-end encrypted.

items.title: Tailscale-aware VP card
items.body: Surfaces the host's tailnet IPs + MagicDNS hostname for paste-into-slicer when you reach BamDude over Tailscale; copy-to-clipboard in one click.

items.title: VP archive name source toggle
items.body: Choose whether VP-routed archives take their print_name from 3MF metadata or the upload filename — per-install setting.

items.title: Obico AI failure detection
items.body: Optional ML-based failure detection with notify / pause / pause-and-power-off responses. Every printer card carries an AI badge — grey while nothing is watched, then green, amber or red as a monitored print is classified — so you can follow it without leaving the Printers page.

groups.title: Auth & Integrations
groups.description: Always-on auth with MFA, OIDC, LDAP, plus REST/MQTT/Prometheus for everything else.

items.title: Granular permissions
items.body: 80+ resource:action permissions, three default groups (Admin / Operator / Viewer).

items.title: TOTP + Email OTP + Backup codes
items.body: Multi-factor auth with backup codes; per-user enrollment, admin-resettable.

items.title: MFA + OIDC secrets encrypted at rest by default
items.body: Auto-bootstrapped Fernet key (env → file → generated, mode 0600) — every TOTP secret + OIDC client_secret encrypted on disk without a manual env-var step. Status dashboard shows key source, encrypted vs legacy plaintext counts, and decryption-broken alerts. Backup ZIP packages the key alongside the DB so a restored install on a fresh host keeps decrypting.

items.title: OIDC SSO incl. Azure Entra ID
items.body: PKCE + state + nonce + JWKS, SSRF guards on issuer URL, configurable email_claim (preferred_username / upn) for Microsoft 365 / Entra ID.

items.title: SSO declared in environment variables
items.body: For compose / Helm / GitOps installs where clicking through Settings once is not part of the deployment. Set four BAMDUDE_OIDC_* variables and the provider is created on startup and reapplied on every restart — shown read-only in Settings, because an edit would be accepted and then silently undone. Removing the variables disables it rather than deleting it, so linked accounts keep their link.

items.title: LDAP / Active Directory
items.body: Group-mapped LDAP login for shops with existing identity.

items.title: Sliding-session refresh
items.body: Rotating refresh tokens, OWASP reuse detection, HttpOnly cookie + 1h access JWT.

items.title: API keys with cloud-access scope
items.body: Per-user `bb_*` tokens scoped to a subset of the owner's permissions. Opt-in cloud-access scope reaches Bambu Cloud routes. X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer — both supported. Hashed at rest, last_used_at surfaced for audit.

items.title: REST + WebSocket API
items.body: Full REST API with API keys, plus WebSocket for live status integrations.

items.title: Prometheus metrics
items.body: Dedicated /metrics endpoint with farm-level and per-printer counters.

items.title: Per-request trace IDs
items.body: Every HTTP request gets an X-Trace-Id header echoed in logs so you can correlate one user action across HTTP / MQTT / scheduler lines.

items.title: MQTT publishing
items.body: Forward printer state to your home MQTT broker for Home Assistant / Node-RED.

items.title: Git backup
items.body: Schedule automatic config backups to GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, or Forgejo — restore from any commit. Per-backend `git_providers/` package handles the API shape divergences (Forgejo plays Gitea-shape; GitHub uses Issues vs GitLab Issues, etc.).

items.title: OrcaSlicer preset import
items.body: Drop your local Orca filament profiles into BamDude in one click.

items.title: In-app bug report
items.body: Floating Bug button on every page — describe the issue, optionally drop a screenshot, click Start Debug Logging, reproduce, then Stop & Submit. Sanitized logs (printer names / serials / IPs / passwords / emails / API keys redacted) + screenshot + structured support snapshot get posted to the bamdude.top relay, which creates a GitHub issue. The relay holds the PAT, BamDude never does.

items.title: In-app updater with stable + beta channels
items.body: Settings → System → Install Update does the full sequence (git fetch --tags, reset --hard to the tag, pip install, npm build) without leaving the UI. Optional Include beta updates toggle surfaces `vX.Y.ZbN` releases too — beta detection is dual-signal (version-name convention OR GitHub prerelease flag). Docker installs aren't auto-applied (running git/pip/npm in a live container would corrupt the image), but the UI shows both image-pull and source-build commands with the resolved tag pre-filled — including a beta-specific hint that `:latest` doesn't track betas, so explicit `image: kainpl/bamdude:0.4.5b1` pinning is required.
